evidence.quote: having for master only his father
By way of teaching him quickly, his masters sent out their new Minister to Russia in the same ship.
turn him into a harsh judge of his masters

adjudications.reason: Paragraph 4 of the revision says the son had 'for master only his father'. Paragraph 5 then says 'his masters sent out their new Minister to Russia'. In the source, those masters are the people he judged harshly, and the revision cut that clause, so 'his masters' now has no antecedent and contradicts paragraph 4. The cut of the palace counterfactual is a tolerable tradeoff, because 'most fortunate ... only his father' still explains the luck. The minimal fix is to replace 'his masters' with 'the Government', which sent Clay according to the source ('Secretary Seward had occasion...').

evidence.quote: he did not then know that Senator Sumner had opposed it
Minister Adams had no friend in the Senate; he could hope for no favors, and he asked none.

adjudications.reason: Paragraph 1 still states Sumner's opposition and the knowledge boundary. 'Had no friend in the Senate; he could hope for no favors, and he asked none' still carries the beat, and chapter 009 has already established the Sumner rupture. Cutting the Seward/Chairman lines is a legitimate compression, not a broken causal link.

evidence.quote: The sentiment of anti-slavery had disappeared.
As for the private secretary himself, he was, like all Bostonians, instinctively English.

adjudications.reason: Paragraph 7 sets up the specific expectation that the young man was going to a friendly, anti-slavery England. The explicit reversal in paragraph 8 was cut, although the plan marks this mistaken belief as essential. The source sentence is short. After the family-effort sentence was cut, 'As for the private secretary himself' contrasts with nothing, so it can be simplified to 'He was'.

evidence.quote: The blow must have fallen within three months, and would then have broken him down.
ready to leave England at once, and never assuming more than three months for their limit

adjudications.reason: The danger is still conveyed elsewhere. Paragraph 11 says the blow 'would then have broken him down', and paragraph 15 says they were 'ready to leave England at once' within a three-month limit. 'Unreflecting confidence' is still proved by 'It never entered his mind that his father might lose his nerve'. Restoring all of this would cost about 50 words against a word budget that is already negative, so this is an acceptable tradeoff.

evidence.quote: They saw the hopeless position they were in if the American Minister made a mistake, and lost no time in expressing to all the world their estimate of his character.
never afterwards deserted him. Monckton Milnes was a social power in London

adjudications.reason: 'The singular luck ... never afterwards deserted him' now has no stated consequence. The sentence explaining why Milnes and Forster publicly backed the Minister is gone, and that support is what earns 'four such allies'. The plan's risk note asks to trim the portraits, not this link. The first draft's single sentence is restored, and the cost is offset by trimming the optional prize-fight elaboration while keeping 'hardest hitters'.

remaining_concerns: The 'go home within a few weeks' horizon from source paragraph 9 remains cut; the closing 'He meant to go home' relies on the three-month horizon in paragraph 15 instead.
